title: sre-weekly-update-2026-06-27
content:
SRE Weekly Update - 2026-06-27
Owner: Samira Patel
Summary: This week focused on stabilizing prefix-cache behavior after the June 22 throughput incident, finalizing the p99 latency SLO calibration, and smoothing on-call handoffs for the new rotation. Overall platform availability stayed within target for the week, but we burned part of the error budget on the cache thrash incident (see incidents).

Highlights:
- Incident response: Mitigations deployed for INC-2026-06-22 (cache thrash) - immediate fixes reduced error rate from 3.4% -> 0.2% within 45 minutes. Full rollout of cache gating shipped on 2026-06-24. Postmortem in progress.
- SLO work: p99 latency calibration proposal accepted; SLOs updated in SLO dashboard and linked to the runbook. Small tweak to alert thresholds (+10% buffer) approved to reduce alert fatigue for known noisy endpoints.
- On-call: New on-call rotation started 2026-06-25. Handoff doc updated with clearer throttling playbook and paging escalation matrix.

Incidents (last 7 days):
1) INC-2026-06-22 - Cache thrash causing elevated 5xxs and tail-latency spikes
   - Timeline: 09:17 UTC - first customer reports, 09:25 UTC - automated alert (error-rate > 2%), 09:35 UTC - on-call acknowledged, 10:20 UTC - mitigation (cache gating + reduced batch size) applied to canary, 10:54 UTC - full rollout, 11:02 UTC - system recovered to baseline.
   - Impact: p99 generation latency increased to ~9.2s (baseline 2.1s) for ~90 minutes; user-facing 5xxs peaked at 3.4%. A subset of customers on large-sequence workloads saw degraded throughput.
   - Root cause hypothesis: regression in prefix-KV eviction ordering interacting with a recent continuous-batching change (PR #1984). Under high churn of short-lived prefixes, KV cache thrash caused excessive memory churn and GC pressure on the runtime host.
   - Actions taken: rolled back partial batching change for affected hosts, applied cache gating (limits concurrent prefix load), patched runtime to add additional metrics around eviction churn.
   - Follow-ups: complete postmortem (confluence:Inc-2026-06-22-cache-thrash-postmortem) due 2026-07-01; SRE-482 tracks follow-up work to add safe defaults and automated circuit-breaker for cache load.

Operational metrics and SLOs:
- Availability: 99.94% (weekly, across hosted-api routes) - within our 99.9% target, but incident consumed ~0.12% of weekly error budget.
- p95 latency (gen): 0.83s (target <= 1.0s)
- p99 latency (gen): 2.1s baseline, spike to 9.2s during incident
- Error rate: 0.18% rollout-week average; peak 3.4% during incident
- Error budget remaining (monthly): ~63% after accounting for this week's burn

Runbooks/Alerts updated this week:
- Adjusted p99 alert threshold and added a new alert for cache-eviction-rate (alerts: s3-cache-eviction-high).
- Throttling runbook updated to include steps for toggling cache gating and reducing batch size; added exact curl commands and IAM service account used by on-call.

On-call handoffs and notes:
- Rotation start: 2026-06-25
- Current on-call: Week A primary - Ethan Kim; Week A secondary - Priya Singh
- Handoff notes:
  - Watch the new cache-eviction-rate alert for early signs; it tends to trigger 10-30m before error-rate climbs.
  - If you see sustained p99 > 4s, initiate throttling runbook and notify product-bench team (Slack: #prod-bench).
  - Escalation matrix: pager -> primary on-call -> SRE lead (Marco) after 20m -> Eng on-call (service owner) after 40m.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- SRE-482 (Samira) - Add eviction-churn metrics to dashboard and implement automatic circuit-breaker for cache load. ETA: 2026-07-08.
- PR review (Marco) - finish review of serving-runtime PR #1984 and add guard rails; block merge until tests added. ETA: 2026-06-30.
- Postmortem (Ethan) - draft postmortem for INC-2026-06-22 and circulate to eng+pm for review. ETA: 2026-07-01.
- Capacity plan (Priya) - reevaluate headroom for large-sequence customers and propose autoscale thresholds; include Dedicated tenant implications. ETA: 2026-07-10.

Planned maintenance and deploys:
- 2026-07-02 02:00-04:00 UTC - rolling upgrade of runtime on c5g-large pools (low-traffic window). Not expected to affect availability but will temporarily reduce capacity; note in status page.
- Serving-runtime: gated deploy of PR #1984 will be reattempted after tests and guard rails added.

Risks and notes for leadership:
- Cache eviction behavior remains our highest near-term reliability risk for large-sequence workloads. We need to prioritize SRE-482 and capacity headroom work to avoid repeat burns.
- Alert fatigue: recent noisy p99 alerts require further tuning - agreed to incrementally widen thresholds and rely more on eviction-rate signal.

Meeting notes (SRE weekly sync - 2026-06-26):
- Attendees: Samira, Ethan, Priya, Marco, Aisha (platform-eng)
- Decisions: Accept p99 calibration proposal; defer unsafe runtime batching changes until guard rails in place; require at least one canary run > 24h for runtime-level changes impacting caching behavior.
- Open items: Define canary acceptance criteria for runtime cache changes (Priya + platform-eng).

Notes to self / scratch:
- Remember to add a short howto for toggling cache gating from the console (very common on-call step).
- Follow-up: check with CS for any customer escalations we haven't logged.

FYI: Links to dashboards and runbooks in linked_artifacts above and pinned in #sre-ops.

-- End of update
